title: Why is the sky blue?
description: Sunlight scatters off the air: why the sky is blue and sunsets red.

shots.title: Blue sky, red sunset
shots.say: Same Sun, same air. So why is the sky blue at noon, and red at sunset?

shots.title: White light, every colour
shots.say: Sunlight looks white, but every colour is in it, from short blue waves to long red ones.

shots.title: Air scatters blue
shots.say: Each tiny molecule of air scatters that light. Blue is scattered about 5 times more than red.

shots.title: Blue from everywhere
shots.say: That scattered blue comes at you from every direction, so the whole sky glows blue.

shots.title: The long sunset path
shots.say: At sunset the Sun is low, and its light crosses about 38 times more air to reach you.

shots.title: Red gets through
shots.say: Along that long path, even more of the blue is scattered away. What reaches you is orange and red.

shots.title: Same air, different path
shots.say: Same air, different path: blue by day, red at dusk.
